# 2 Kings Chapter 3 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 223v–224v | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/2KI_003_page_001.jpg, 2KI_003_page_002.jpg, 2KI_003_page_003.jpg

---

**1** Jehoram son of Ahab became king of Israel in Samaria in the eighteenth year of King Jehoshaphat of Judah, and he reigned twelve years.

**2** He did what was evil in the LORD's sight — though not as badly as his father and mother, since he did remove the sacred pillar of Baal that his father had set up.

**3** Still, he held on to the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who had led Israel into sin. He never abandoned them.

**4** Now King Mesha of Moab was a sheep breeder who paid tribute to the king of Israel: a hundred thousand lambs and the wool of a hundred thousand rams every year.

**5** But after Ahab died, the king of Moab rebelled against Israel.

**6** King Jehoram immediately set out from Samaria and mobilized the entire Israelite army.

**7** He sent word to King Jehoshaphat of Judah: "The king of Moab has rebelled against me. Will you join me in attacking Moab?" Jehoshaphat replied, "I'm with you — my troops are your troops, my horses are your horses."

**8** "Which route should we take?" Jehoram asked. "Through the wilderness of Edom," Jehoshaphat answered.

**9** So the king of Israel marched out with the king of Judah and the king of Edom. After seven days of marching through the desert, there was no water left for the army or the pack animals.

**10** "This is disaster!" the king of Israel cried. "The LORD has lured us three kings out here just to hand us over to Moab!"

**11** But Jehoshaphat asked, "Isn't there a prophet of the LORD here we can consult?" One of the Israelite king's officers answered, "Elisha son of Shaphat is here — the one who served as Elijah's attendant."

**12** "The word of the LORD is with him," Jehoshaphat confirmed. So all three kings went down to see Elisha.

**13** Elisha said to the king of Israel, "What do you want with me? Go ask your father's prophets or your mother's prophets." But the king of Israel said, "No — the LORD is the one who called us three kings out here to be handed over to Moab."

**14** Elisha replied, "As surely as the LORD of Hosts lives, the God I serve — if I didn't respect King Jehoshaphat of Judah, I wouldn't even glance in your direction.

**15** Now bring me a musician." While the musician played, the power of the LORD came upon Elisha.

**16** He said, "This is what the LORD says: 'Dig this valley full of trenches.'

**17** For the LORD says: 'You will see no wind, you will see no rain — yet this valley will fill with water, and you will drink, you and your livestock and your pack animals.'

**18** This is easy for the LORD. He will also hand Moab over to you.

**19** You will destroy every fortified city and every fine town. You will cut down every productive tree, block every spring, and ruin every good field with stones."

**20** The next morning, at the hour of the morning sacrifice, water came flowing from the direction of Edom until the whole landscape was flooded.

**21** Meanwhile, all the Moabites had heard that the kings were marching against them. Everyone old enough to carry a weapon was called up and stationed along the border.

**22** When they got up early that morning and the sun hit the water, it looked blood-red from where the Moabites stood.

**23** "That's blood!" they shouted. "The kings must have turned on each other — they've slaughtered each other! Come on, Moab — grab the plunder!"

**24** But when they reached the Israelite camp, the Israelites charged out and routed them. They chased the fleeing Moabites deep into their own territory, cutting them down as they went.

**25** They demolished the cities. Every soldier threw stones on every productive field until it was buried. They blocked every spring and cut down every fruit tree. Only Kir-hareseth was left standing, and the slingers surrounded it and hammered it.

**26** When the king of Moab realized the battle was lost, he gathered seven hundred swordsmen and tried to break through the lines toward the king of Edom, but they failed.

**27** Then he took his firstborn son — his heir to the throne — and sacrificed him as a burnt offering on the city wall. A terrible fury fell upon Israel, and they pulled back from him and returned home.

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

**Verse 4 — Mesha:** This is the same King Mesha known from the famous Moabite Stone (discovered in 1868), which tells this rebellion story from the Moabite perspective. Mesha credits his god Chemosh for the victory — a remarkable parallel to Israel's crediting YHWH.

**Verse 11 — "served as Elijah's attendant":** Literally "poured water on Elijah's hands." This was the mark of a personal servant. Elisha is introduced not by his miracles but by his humble service.

**Verse 22 — Red water:** The morning sun on water can create a blood-red reflection — a natural phenomenon the narrator uses to spring the trap. What Moab reads as evidence of chaos is actually the sign of divine provision.

**Verse 27 — The sacrifice:** This is one of the most disturbing and deliberately unexplained verses in the Bible. The king sacrifices his own son on the wall. "A terrible fury" — whose? The Hebrew *qetsef gadol* refuses to name its source. The narrator will not explain why Israel withdraws after witnessing this act. The silence is the theology.

*— PNEUMA*
